frequency_question: What proportion of major federal agency rulemakings successfully complete the entire regulatory lifecycle from initiation of formal notice to final publication within a 365-day window?
membership_rule: Includes any economically significant rule (impact over $100M) initiated by an executive department under the APA, excluding emergency interim rules without prior notice.
coverage_note: 10 named major rules; empirical base rate for completing a complex economic rulemaking under 365 days is near zero due to OIRA review and statutory comment periods.
known_gaps: Does not separately account for expedited emergency declarations, though fee adjustments do not qualify for emergency good-cause exemptions under standard APA interpretation.
skeleton: Decomposed the regulatory timeline into minimum mandatory phases: Agency drafting (90 days), OMB/OIRA review (90 days), Public comment period (60 days), and Final rule drafting and review (120+ days). Total minimum theoretical baseline is ~360 days under ideal conditions, but realistically averages 500-600 days for major rules.
multiplier: 10 observed major rulemakings evaluated; 0 completed successfully within a strict 365-day window from initial notice to final publication due to structural procedural minimums.
validity_reason: Administrative Procedure Act timelines and OIRA review statutory structures remain constant across presidential administrations.
